title: Bounded cleanup of a visited tape
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $x$ and $w$ be Boolean words, let $p$ be an input-head position for $w$, let $T$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $i$ be a work-tape index of $M$. Write $d$ for the content of tape $i$ after $M$ runs on $x$ for $T$ steps, write $\ell$ and $h$ for the least and greatest head positions of that tape up to time $T$, and let the interval marker be true on $[\ell,h]$ and blank elsewhere; place a single origin marker at cell $0$, and start the three-tape cleaner with all heads at the head position of tape $i$ at time $T$. There is a time $t$ with $0<t\le 6T+7$ such that the cleaner is not in state $3$ at any time $j<t$, and at time $t$ it is in state $3$ with all three tapes blank and all heads at the origin.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over Booleans
replaced:
Let $M$ be a machine, $x$ an input, $T$ a time, and $i$ a work tape. Then there is a
positive time $t \le 6T + 7$ such that the interval cleaner, started on the actual tape
$i$ of the run of $M$ at time $T$ with its visited-span and origin markers, does not
visit its return state before $t$ and at time $t$ is exactly the blank-endpoint return
configuration with all heads at the origin.
